title: autotune: default batching/caching and quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (was failing on first run)
description: Context: we've seen steady opportunity to reduce per-token costs by tuning defaults for batching/caching and surfacing quantization profiles automatically. This PR implements an experiment-first rollout: 1) default batching and prefix/KV caching heuristics applied at the router/runtime level; 2) a quantization profile registry with fallback compatibility rules; 3) unit-economics (UEcon) tooling to estimate expected cost impact per route/model; and 4) a small console integration to display suggested savings and apply recommended profiles. Motivation: teams often leave batching/cache defaults conservative, and customers don't have an easy way to estimate unit economics before rollouts. This PR reduces manual tuning and provides safer automated recommendations.
commits: feat(autotune): add default batching heuristics + knob to opt-out
feat(kv-cache): prefix caching TTL and hit-rate estimator
feat(quant-registry): quant profiles, compatibility rules, and auto-suggest API
feat(uecon): cost estimator service + CLI utility
chore(console): show suggested savings on model page (UI hook only)
test: add unit/integration tests for estimator and fallback logic
fix(ci): reorder integration suite to avoid transient GPU allocation failures

release_notes:
- Add default batching heuristics to improve throughput while preserving latency SLOs.
- Enable prefix/KV caching with hit-rate estimator and TTL heuristics.
- Introduce quantization profile registry with compatibility-aware fallbacks.
- Add UEcon tooling (service + CLI) to estimate per-route cost impact and expected savings.
- Console hook to surface suggested savings on model profile pages (opt-in).
